AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Vegetables? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Vegetables.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Vegetables.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Vegetables.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Vegetables.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.

12. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Wild Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Growing Vegetables and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — newton (N)

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. D — Ice melting to water

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Vegetables.

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.

12. D — Producers

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Conservation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Conserving Wild Animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Growing Vegetables; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
